html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit

  • Progressive summarization risks and the "case facts" block
  • The "lost in the middle" effect and how to place information
  • How tool results swell the context, and how to trim them
  • Context degradation in long sessions, scratchpad files, subagent delegation, manifests and /compact

2Keeping Critical Facts Alive (Task 5.1)

Running case

Birchwood Supply's Long Support Chat

  • A customer chats for an hour about three issues: a late order, a duplicate charge and a damaged item
  • After several summarizations, the agent forgets the exact refund amount ($84.50), the promised date (12 March) and which order goes with which problem
  • Each lookup_order call returns 40+ fields, but only five matter for returns
Risk What happens Remedy
Progressive summarization Numbers, percentages, dates and customer-stated expectations become vague ("a refund was discussed") Keep transactional facts in a persistent "case facts" block outside the summarized history, included in every prompt
Multi-issue sessions Facts of different issues blend together Extract structured issue data (order IDs, amounts, statuses) into a separate context layer
Tool-result bloat 40+ fields per lookup eat tokens out of proportion to their value Trim each result to the relevant fields before it accumulates
"Lost in the middle" Models reliably use the beginning and end of a long input but may omit findings from the middle Put a key-findings summary at the start; organize details under explicit section headers
Context limits of downstream agents A verbose upstream result overruns the next agent Have upstream agents return structured data (key facts, citations, relevance scores) instead of long text and reasoning chains
Lost provenance Synthesis cannot tell where facts came from Require subagents to include metadata (dates, source locations, methodological context) in structured outputs 

CASE FACTS (verbatim, never summarize)
- Customer: C-48213 (verified)
- Issue 1: order 77102, late, promised 12 March
- Issue 2: order 77102, duplicate charge $84.50, status: refund pending
- Issue 3: order 77310, damaged item, photo received
  • The API is stateless: to keep a conversation coherent you must send the complete conversation history (plus your case-facts block) in each request to maintain conversational coherence.

Exam tip

Customer's exact amounts and dates keep disappearing? → a persistent case-facts block outside the summary. Do not "summarize more carefully".

Exam tip

Exact amounts and dates lost in a long chat call for a case-facts block outside the summary, not "summarize better".

3Exploring Large Codebases (Task 5.4)

Case (continued): An engineer explores Birchwood's 3,000-file monorepo for hours. After a while Claude begins to say "this probably uses the typical repository pattern" instead of naming the specific classes it found earlier.

  • Context degradation: in extended sessions the model gives inconsistent answers and refers to "typical patterns" instead of the specific classes discovered earlier.
Technique How it helps
Scratchpad files The agent writes key findings to a file and references it for subsequent questions, so facts survive context boundaries
Subagent delegation Spawn subagents for specific questions ("find all test files", "trace the refund flow's dependencies"); the verbose output stays in their context and the main agent keeps high-level coordination
Phase summaries Summarize key findings of one phase before spawning subagents for the next, and inject the summary into their initial context
State manifests (crash recovery) Each agent exports its state to a known location; the coordinator loads a manifest on resume and injects the state into agent prompts
/compact Reduces context usage when it fills with verbose discovery output

[Verify live] Current documentation: a subagent returns only its final message to the parent, so its detailed tool calls stay out of the parent's context; when the context window nears its limit, Claude Code and the Agent SDK compact automatically (older turns are summarized), and instructions that must persist belong in CLAUDE.md, which is re-loaded. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Long exploration drifting to "typical patterns" calls for a scratchpad file and subagents, and /compact when verbose output fills the context.

4Exam Q&A

S1After many turns, Birchwood's agent forgets the exact refund amount and a promised date because earlier turns were summarized. What is the best fix?

  • AKeep the amounts, dates and order numbers in a persistent case-facts block included in every prompt, outside the summarized history
  • BIncrease the temperature
  • CAsk the summarizer to be more concise and to keep only the most important sentences of each turn
  • DDelete the conversation history
Show the answer

Answer: A. Transactional facts must not pass through progressive summarization.

S2A customer discusses three issues in one chat, and the agent mixes up which order has which problem. What helps?

  • AExtract structured issue data into a separate context layer
  • BHandle only the first issue
  • CUse a longer system prompt
  • DAsk the customer to start again and handle one issue per conversation
Show the answer

Answer: A. A separate structured layer keeps each issue's facts distinct.

S3An order lookup returns 40+ fields, but only five are relevant for returns, and the context fills quickly. What is the best approach?

  • AKeep everything, in case it is needed later
  • BSummarize each lookup into one sentence
  • CTrim the result to the relevant fields before it is added to the context
  • DDisable the tool
Show the answer

Answer: C. Trimming keeps relevant data and prevents token waste.

S4An aggregated research input of 30 findings is passed to a synthesis agent, which tends to omit findings from the middle. What mitigates this?

  • ASend the findings one at a time, each in a separate request, and merge the answers
  • BRemove the headers
  • CShuffle the findings randomly
  • DPut a key-findings summary first and organize the rest under section headers
Show the answer

Answer: D. Models attend best to the start and end; a summary first and clear headers reduce loss in the middle.

S5A subagent returns paragraphs of reasoning, but the downstream synthesis agent has a small context budget. What should change?

  • ARemove citations
  • BMake the upstream agent return structured facts, citations and relevance scores
  • CReturn the raw tool output as well
  • DAsk the synthesis agent to read faster and to skip the longest paragraphs on its own
Show the answer

Answer: B. Structured, compact upstream output fits a limited downstream budget while keeping attribution.

S6During a long exploration, the agent starts to answer with "typical patterns" rather than the specific classes it found earlier. Which combination counters this?

  • ADisable all tools
  • BAsk the same question again
  • CScratchpad files for key findings plus subagents for verbose exploration
  • DRead every file again in the same session to refresh everything it knew before
Show the answer

Answer: C. Persisting findings and isolating verbose output keep specifics available and context lean.

S7Which TWO practices keep critical facts alive in a long support conversation? Select TWO.

  • ADeleting the history after each reply
  • BSummarizing everything more aggressively
  • CKeeping all 40 fields of every lookup
  • DTrimming tool output to the relevant fields
  • EA persistent case-facts block outside the summarized history
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Verbatim facts and lean tool output protect important details. Heavier summarization and bloated results make things worse.

S8Which TWO help counter context degradation in a long codebase exploration? Select TWO.

  • ADisabling all tools
  • BAsking the same question again
  • CRe-reading every file in the same session
  • DDelegating verbose searches to subagents
  • EScratchpad files for key findings
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Persisting findings and isolating verbose exploration keep specifics available and context small.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Summarization risk Amounts, dates, expectations get vague → case-facts block outside the summary
Multi-issue Separate structured issue layer
Tool output Trim to relevant fields (5 of 40+)
Position effect Beginning and end are reliable; middle is not → summary first + section headers
Upstream agents Return structured facts, citations, relevance scores, with metadata (dates, sources)
Statelessness Send the complete history each request
Degradation "Typical patterns" instead of specific classes → scratchpad, subagents, phase summaries
Recovery State exports + manifest loaded by the coordinator on resume
/compact Reduce context when verbose discovery fills it
